name: ztpf_author_render_interface_descriptions
why: The whole authoring loop, proven by its output: the chat writes a template that reads device data, saves it, and renders it on a device through 'Render Script - Template'.

The rendered text is compared with an expectation computed in plain Python from the same device's data, collected by a separate 'Get Metadata Source Data on Device' run. Offline, test_template rendered against an empty context and always passed.
The analyst has a different template open, so the render must run on the new one (runs_on); an update of the open template is rejected and fails the row.

steps.user: Create a new Text template named 'Live Writes - Physical Interface Descriptions', linked to the 'DeviceDB System Interfaces - Physical' metadata source so it gets data.dvmdb_ints_physical. It must output one `config system interface` block that ends with `end`. Inside it, for every physical interface whose ip address is not 0.0.0.0, sorted by name: `edit "<name>"`, then `set description "<alias, or the name when there is no alias> on <device name>"` (the device name is record.device.name), then `set allowaccess <the allowaccess values separated by spaces>` (allowaccess can be a list or a single string; leave the line out when it is empty), then `next`. Skip interfaces with no ip. Test it against the source's example data before saving.
Now render 'Live Writes - Physical Interface Descriptions' on a real device with the Render Script - Template playbook.
